topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and cellular context of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as the evolution of mutation-bearing cells whose progression depends on genetic susceptibility and a permissive cellular environment.

topics.label: Evidence and uncertainty surrounding environmental cancer risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental contributions to cancer risk are recognised and interpreted despite uncertainty about individual outcomes.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the interaction between pathogens and cellular changes.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce mutation-causing DNA damage, often through the body's own metabolic processes.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require subsequent promotion before tumours develop.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: The developmental examples and concluding recap explain how the biological context of exposure determines susceptibility to carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how researchers obtain evidence linking exposures to cancer and why that evidence has methodological limitations.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: The closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and their implications for everyday risk–benefit decisions.
